o1.biggest_strength: It makes the right call immediately: do not cut to 20%, fix credit and payouts, and spend the partner manager’s time on the top creator-educators.
o1.biggest_mistake: Some of the projected cost maths for the 90-day window is a bit too confident from the data given, and the date-specific 30-day plan would need checking before sending.
o1.what_would_make_it_a_10: Tighten the assumptions behind the extra commission forecast, remove any speculative numbers that cannot be defended, and make the rollout dates generic or confirmed.

o2.biggest_strength: It clearly explains why the 20% cut is risky, using the break-even revenue drop, top-20 concentration, churn, and lifetime value in a way finance would understand.
o2.biggest_mistake: The 40% first-year Partner tier adds cost and complexity when the data says the real problems are lost credit and slow payouts, not the headline rate.
o2.what_would_make_it_a_10: Keep 30% for both tiers, use the tier for service and payout advantages instead of a higher commission, and sharpen the cost forecast for the new 90-day window.

reason: I would rather use Output 1 because it solves the real problem without creating a new commission problem. Output 2 is strong, but the 40% tier feels like paying more for an issue we can fix with tracking, payouts, and better partner care.
